intro.author: Paul, with Timothy named as co-sender (1:1)
intro.audience: The church at Corinth and believers throughout the province of Achaia (1:1)
intro.setting: After 1 Corinthians, Paul's relationship with the church grew strained. He made a painful visit (2:1), then wrote a sorrowful letter 'with many tears' (2:4) and waited anxiously for Titus to report back. Titus finally met him in Macedonia with encouraging news (7:6-7), but rival teachers in Corinth were still questioning Paul's authority. Many scholars think the book may combine more than one of Paul's letters, especially chapters 10–13, though this is debated.
intro.purpose: Paul writes to restore trust, explain the nature of his ministry, encourage the church to complete its gift for Jerusalem, and answer rivals who belittled him.
intro.bigIdea: God's power is shown most clearly through human weakness.

outline.title: The ministry of the new covenant

commentary.t: THE SECOND EPISTLE OF PAUL THE APOSTLE TO THE CORINTHIANS
